In a warehouse demonstration, a wooden crate A of mass \(m_A\) slides on a rough loading ramp that rises to the right at an angle \(\theta\) above the horizontal. A taut, massless, inextensible rope runs parallel to the ramp from the crate, passes over a fixed, frictionless, massless pulley at the upper right end, and then runs vertically downward to a freely hanging sandbag B of mass \(m_B\).

The coefficient of kinetic friction between the crate and the ramp is \(\mu_k\). **At the instant shown, the crate is moving up the incline and speeding up.** It remains in contact with the ramp.
items.glossary_markdown:
Let \(T\) be the rope-tension magnitude, \(N\) the normal-force magnitude on A, \(g\) the magnitude of gravitational acceleration, and \(a_A>0\) the magnitude of A’s acceleration. The unit vectors \(\hat{\imath}\) and \(\hat{\jmath}\) point along the positive \(x\) and \(y\) axes shown in the figure.

**Which equation correctly expresses Newton’s second law for object A in the coordinate system shown?**

feedback_by_choice.A: Correct. Tension, parallel gravity, and kinetic friction have the appropriate signs, the normal acceleration is zero, and the acceleration is along \(+x\).
feedback_by_choice.B: The acceleration sign is reversed. A is moving along \(+x\) and speeding up, so \(\vec{a}_A=+a_A\hat{\imath}\).
feedback_by_choice.C: The parallel component of gravity is missing. The weight has a nonzero component along the incline: \(-m_A g\sin\theta\).
feedback_by_choice.D: The acceleration has been projected using the incline angle even though the coordinate axes are already aligned with the incline. A stays on the straight surface, so \(a_y=0\).
feedback_by_choice.E: The parallel component of gravity has the wrong sign. Gravity points down the incline, opposite \(+x\), so its \(x\) component is \(-m_A g\sin\theta\).
feedback_by_choice.F: The friction sign is reversed. A moves along \(+x\), so kinetic friction acts along \(-x\): \(\vec{f}_k=-\mu_k N\hat{\imath}\).

items.feedback_figure_alt: Free-body diagram of isolated object A. Tension points uphill toward the right, the normal force is perpendicular to and outward from the incline, weight points vertically down, and kinetic friction points downhill, opposite the motion. Above A, a solid velocity arrow points uphill toward the right; a dashed acceleration arrow points uphill toward the right. The coordinate axes originate on A: positive x points right along the incline and positive y points perpendicular and outward. A dotted guide extends in the negative y direction. The acute angle theta is marked between this negative y direction and the vertically downward weight.

In a laboratory demonstration, a wooden block A of mass \(m_A\) slides on a rough inclined board that falls to the right at an angle \(\theta\) below the horizontal. A taut, massless, inextensible rope runs parallel to the board from the block, passes over a fixed, frictionless, massless pulley at the lower right end, and then runs vertically downward to a freely hanging object B of mass \(m_B\). The hanging rope and object B clear the board and its support.

The coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the board is \(\mu_k\). **At the instant shown, the block is sliding down the incline and speeding up.** It remains in contact with the board.
